title: Mara and the Tide
premise: Edmund Blackwood fled a coastal town and a devastating betrayal fifteen years ago, reinventing themselves as a meticulous marine biologist who counts turtles and trusts no one with the whole truth. When a letter postmarked eleven years ago—written by their first love, Mara Voss, before her disappearance—surfaces in a donated archive, Edmund returns to the town of Salt Hollow to find out what really happened. There they discover Mara is alive, hiding under another name, having faked her death to escape a dangerous family debt that would have destroyed them both. As old love reignites and the truth about who betrayed whom finally surfaces, Edmund must choose between exposing Mara's secret to clear their own long-stained name or keeping silent and losing her again; in the end, they burn the letter together, testify to a partial truth that frees them both, and build a life on the tide line where belonging costs everything but is finally worth it.
about_author: Tamsin Thackeray is a former lighthouse keeper's daughter who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck archives along the Cornish coast before turning to fiction. She writes romances about people who mistake survival for living, usually within earshot of the sea.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. On a research station in the Hebrides, Edmund counts hatchlings with obsessive precision, a life built on small safe steps after fifteen years of exile from Salt Hollow. A colleague's casual question about home cracks something open. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness masquerading as peace.

chapters.title: The Postmark
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. An archivist emails: a letter addressed to Edmund, postmarked eleven years ago, found in a donated estate collection. The sender's name is Mara Voss—the woman declared dead at sea a decade ago. Edmund reads it three times without breathing. Emotional beat: the past arriving like a body washed ashore.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, interwoven with the letter's text. Mara wrote that she was leaving, that someone had threatened Edmund's life if she stayed, and that she'd rather be mourned than be the reason he was buried. Edmund books passage to Salt Hollow. Emotional beat: grief reorganizing itself into hope.

chapters.title: Salt Hollow
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Returning after fifteen years, Edmund finds the town half-remembered and half-hostile; old neighbors stare, and the harbor wall still bears the scar of the storm the night Mara vanished. Emotional beat: exile ending, but belonging not yet earned.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Daughter
chapters.summary: Nell's POV (introduced). Nell Okafor, the young archivist whose donation surfaced the letter, meets Edmund at the ferry and offers help—she grew up on stories of the Voss disappearance. Her curiosity is genuine but her methods are reckless. Emotional beat: an ally who may become a liability.

chapters.title: A Woman Called Wren
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Following a thread from the letter's paper stock, Edmund tracks a bookbinder in a neighboring cove known locally as Wren—who moves like Mara, laughs like Mara, and flinches when Edmund says her real name aloud. Emotional beat: recognition across a workbench, terror and tenderness colliding.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Mara/Wren's POV. Mara explains nothing yet, but we see her life: forged papers, a locked box under the floorboards, nightly checks of the tide tables. She has survived by never staying anywhere longer than two years—and Edmund's arrival breaks every rule she lives by. Emotional beat: survival exposed as its own kind of prison.

chapters.title: The Debt
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flashback: the Voss family owed a violent smuggling syndicate; Mara was to be married off to settle it. Faking her death during the storm was her father's plan and her only escape—but it meant letting Edmund believe she chose to abandon him. Emotional beat: the price of survival made concrete.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund and Mara circle each other for days—she repairs his grandmother's broken compass, he brings her turtle eggs to incubate. They trade truths in increments, neither giving the whole heart. Emotional beat: love resuming exactly where caution left off.

chapters.title: Nell Asks Too Many Questions
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell cross-references the letter with shipping records and realizes 'Wren' arrived in the cove weeks after Mara Voss drowned. She confronts Edmund, who lies badly. Nell, hurt, starts drafting an article. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth beginning to pull apart.

chapters.title: The Man from the Syndicate
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A stranger named Corrigan appears in Salt Hollow asking after a woman with a bookbinder's hands. Edmund recognizes the syndicate's collector from the old days and realizes Mara's death faked eleven years ago is about to stop working. Emotional beat: time running out made literal.

chapters.title: Run With Me
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Edmund proposes what Mara always refused: run together, new names, the Hebrides station, turtles and anonymity. For one night she almost says yes—they sleep tangled in the loft above the bindery, whole hearts lent at last. Emotional beat: the brief, dangerous sweetness of choosing each other.

chapters.title: Why I Stayed Dead
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At dawn Mara refuses: running means Edmund inherits her debt forever, and the syndicate punishes families, not just debtors. Staying invisible kept Edmund safe; loving him openly will get him killed. She asks him to leave. Emotional beat: sacrifice weaponized against love.

chapters.title: The Betrayal Reversed
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Devastated, Edmund digs into the old case and discovers the truth Mara doesn't know: it wasn't her father who arranged the fake death—it was Edmund's own brother, who sold the plan to the syndicate and pocketed the money, then let Edmund take the town's blame. Emotional beat: fifteen years of self-blame collapsing into fury.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Harbor House
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund faces his brother Julian, now a respectable harbormaster, and demands the truth. Julian admits it with chilling calm: the syndicate still holds his ledger, which means Mara can never be safe while he's free. Emotional beat: the betrayer revealed as a coward, not a mastermind.

chapters.title: Nell Publishes
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Cornered by a rival journalist, Nell publishes early: 'Drowned Woman Alive in Coastal Cove.' The story detonates. Corrigan mobilizes; Mara packs to run alone; Edmund races through the storm-dark streets to reach her first. Emotional beat: the truth arriving as catastrophe instead of rescue.

chapters.title: The Tide Line
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Corrigan corners Mara on the flats at low tide, the same ground where she 'died.' Edmund arrives and puts himself between them, offering the one thing the syndicate values more than debts: Julian's ledger, evidence enough to put the syndicate's local network away. Emotional beat: courage replacing flight.

chapters.title: What We Burned
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In the aftermath, with Corrigan detained and Julian arrested, Edmund and Mara burn the original letter on the beach—not to erase the past but to stop it dictating the future. Mara chooses to reclaim her name publicly, testimony given, debt dissolved by the syndicate's collapse. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into ceremony.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund gives a statement that clears both their names, admitting fifteen years of silence and what it cost. The town's reaction is mixed—some forgive, some don't—and Edmund accepts that belonging isn't unanimous approval. Emotional beat: accountability as the final step home.

chapters.title: Hatchlings
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Nesting season on Salt Hollow's restored beach: Mara and Edmund release hatchlings together, her hands steady over his, the first season she hasn't watched the road for strangers. Nell, forgiven, writes a different kind of story. Emotional beat: tenderness without vigilance, for the first time.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund formally joins the coastal restoration project, unpacks boxes that were never fully packed, and stops counting things as a way of not feeling them. A quiet chapter of ordinary domesticity—arguments about curtains, shared coffee, Mara learning the turtle data by heart. Emotional beat: safety chosen daily rather than inherited.

chapters.title: Mara and the Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, closing scene. One year later, on the anniversary of the night Mara 'died,' they walk the tide line at dusk and read the burned letter's last line from memory: 'Love me alive or let me go.' They have done both, and chosen alive. Emotional beat: belonging won, priced honestly, and kept.
